title: Chapter 8 — Baba Oko at Seventy
description: Every politician in the ward is invited to the godfather's seventieth birthday. Nobody is invited to leave early.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Baba Oko is seventy. The party fills Rich Street: three canopies, two live bands, a cake shaped like his house. Every politician in the ward is here, smiling at each other like knives.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: You are not his candidate, but you are invited. That is how he tells you he is still watching. Go. Smile. Leave alive.

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: (at home, earlier) I am not coming. I will not kneel to that man's cake.

variants.text: (at home, earlier) After the envelope? I am not coming. But go. See him with your own eyes, so you remember.

beats.speaker: babaOko
beats.text: (on a throne-shaped chair) Teacher! My boy! (Or "the Teacher who thinks he has feet", depending on who is listening.) Come. What did you bring me?

beats.speaker: babaOko
beats.text: Everyone is watching the gift table.

options.text: A framed photo of the market women, with a note: "They are the ward."
Prostrate flat in front of everybody.

beats.speaker: babaOko
beats.text: (laughing) Dance for me, Teacher! The big men of this ward always dance for me on my birthday!

won.toast: The band sings your name. Baba Oko sprays you with dollar notes. Your agbada has never been so heavy.

lost.toast: Chief Lanre dances like he has done this every year. He has.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Behind the generator, away from the music, Owó Ńlá is smoking. He doesn't smoke. He is smoking anyway.

beats.speaker: owoNla
beats.text: Seventy years. Thirty of them owning this ward. Do you know what he gives for his birthday, Teacher? A list. Who danced, who didn't, who brought what.

beats.speaker: owoNla
beats.text: He offers you a cigarette. You don't smoke either.

options.text: "Why do you still dance for him?"
Take the cigarette. Stand with him in silence.

beats.speaker: owoNla
beats.text: Because the alternative to dancing is a long trip abroad. Or a short trip to the cemetery. (He drops the cigarette.) Enjoy the cake. It's very good. He makes sure.

beats.title: Baba Oko at Seventy
beats.summary: You brought a gift, danced or didn't, and stood with your opponent behind a generator. The godfather wrote everything down.
